reviews.text: I'm a long-time user and all my paid lifetime premium features were taken away when they moved to subscription. Really shocked and disappointed.

reviews.title: In-app purchases gone after update
reviews.text: I couldn't report this issue to the Aloe Bud site because its broken. I bought the Reminders Bundle awhile back which included the icon packs and custom reminders, but when I opened the app after updating it there is now a page that offers me a monthly or annual subscription and at the bottom where I clicked "restore purchases" I got a message that says "nothing to restore". I hope the developers aren't purposefully taking away features people have already paid for because that would be unfair and shady.

reviews.title: Personal Experience
reviews.text:
I have been always using this app to keep track of my certain habits and had always helped to give me motivation, especially whenever I looked at the previous logs of my check-ins. 
However, a few months ago the logs page became completely empty with just lines. 
When I tried fixing this by updating to the latest version, the empty logs still persist. This is really frustrating for me and I’d appreciate if it could be fixed, otherwise I have NO reason to keep this app. I’m on iOS 18 if this helps.

reviews.title: perfect and simple, never overwhelming
reviews.text: i’ve been a huge fan of this app for over 5 years now. it has the perfect and simple interface while still being aesthetically pleasing. the reminders are so sweet and gentle, and you can set them for anything you could possibly need. i’ve used it throughout college, my career, and my mental health journey overall so much to the point where it just feels like part of me. even better is that even though there’s a paywall for certain features, the app is still perfectly functional without it AND they offer a free membership for those who are low income. i’ve never seen any app truly take that much HONEST care of just helping people get (even the simplest) care regardless of their income. i feel like a lot of developers should follow in their footsteps as all mental health care should be able to be afforded by anyone who needs it and this team actually puts their money where their mouth is. absolutely amazing.

reviews.title: Enjoyable App
reviews.text: I love Aloe Bud! For a good few months I did not use it and it is still the best habit "tracker" in terms of motivation and mental health in my experience. The content and themes are very simple making it easy to navigate and use. Aloe Bud also includes a lot of adorable free content, I do not pay for the in-app purchases but even without them you can fully use and get benefits from this app. Being able to choose the difference between an activity of writing/ answering a question and simply clicking a button also helps to keep me from getting bored or overwhelmed with the notifications. Overall really enjoyable app!

reviews.title: Love but distressing bug- please fix!!
reviews.text: As another reviewer said, I have been using this app for years and love the simple layout, the design, and how well it serves its purpose. It keeps me grounded and reminds me to do basic tasks in a cute, fun way when the rest of my phone can be a distraction. I was proud of the history I had logged, but recently it stopped showing anything when I click on the log book: just a blank white screen, regardless of whether I add new logs. So disappointing after the emotional support scrolling through the history of my self-care used to give. Please, please fix this!

reviews.title: Progress deleted- be aware!
reviews.text:
I've used this app for so many purposes for the past few years, but mainly as a journal to keep track of my thoughts. I loved going back and reading my thoughts and seeing my growth.
Recently, a bug on the app was preventing me from seeing any of my past entries. Because there's no way to attach the data to any email or have a backup, when I tried rebooting the app, all of my progress was gone. I've had stuff saved for well over four years.
It was really disheartening to see all of it go away, so I won't use the app again. But other than now, this was the biggest problem I faced with the app.
It still had great features, but keep in mind that anything you write down you should note somewhere else too in case this happens to you too.

reviews.title: Room for improvement
reviews.text:
Update: 
I have started using this app again to see if anything changed, and to my surprise, they listened to my suggestion! Maybe it wasn’t only me complaining though, lol. I bumped my review up by one star. Aside from that problem I had, nothing else has really changed. I’ve been using it as I had a few years ago. So, another suggestion if you’re still listening!: 

The activities stay “completed” (white background) for too long. The next day, they’re still “completed”. Most activities I’d like to complete daily, so it’s disappointing that I can only check things off after two days. That in-between day, I don’t get as much satisfaction as when I can visually see them get lit up. Maybe only keep them lit up for 12 hours? Or give users the option to manually reset each activity, or reset all! Thanks for listening, devs! Sorry for being picky, lol!

reviews.title: Exactly what I needed
reviews.text:
Aloe Bud is super cute, easy to use, and simple — providing the exact level of features that I need to track my self-care habits throughout the day (such as hydration, reading, learning, food). 

A few suggestions to make the app even better though:
• customize or create your own activities
• edit (date/time, note) and delete activity entries — especially for this one, the app automatically makes you enter a “breathe” activity when you first download the app. I mean yes, I did breathe, but as someone who did not want to log breathe as an activity, it was slightly annoying to have that be my first entry.

reviews.title: Thoughtful, Sweet Little Habit Tracker
reviews.text: I downloaded Aloe Bud a few years ago and I don’t remember why I stopped using it. I’ve been in a rut lately and decided to give it another try. I adore the simplicity, design, and ease of this app. It’s cute and very easy to use. I feel like the cuteness helps me remember to use it! The one-time price to unlock the custom reminders is amazing, as I’m so sick of everything asking me for a subscription. I’ve tried so many self-help apps that feel like a weird coaching experience and that’s just not what I’m looking for. I especially love the little reminder not to overly schedule alerts, because I’ve definitely done that before and it gets old so fast. Just want to say thank you to the developers for really nailing it with this app.

reviews.title: Simple and Effective
reviews.text: Aloe Bud is a simple but effective app geared towards improving and managing one’s mental health. The breathing activity is automatically included as a pre-set. Breathing exercises have been proven to reduce stress and anxiety. They can also act as a way to look inward and be aware of one’s breathing patterns. They reduce fight or flight response and improve focus. The app also has activities such as medication reminders. I think this would be very beneficial for anyone who has to take medication for their depression, anxiety, or anything else. It keeps everything relating to your mental health in one place. I personally find the hydrate and fuel activities very helpful. I have a hard time eating/drinking enough when I have classes and work all day. This helps me keep track of when and what I eat. With all of the activities you can set reminders to do them. Once completed, you can hit the “check in” or “complete” button to log the activity. The app itself is visually appealing and well designed. I also appreciate that there is a link to mental health resources such as the Suicide Prevention Lifeline, the Trevor Project, and various more aimed at supporting those with mental illnesses.
